Chapter 14INPUT

The Outer Circuit

Keep moving, and the edge of the city holds.

The seawall looks like a path. It is also the edge of the city, and edges have to be checked. Every walker, runner and cyclist on the seawall, and every person who cannot sleep and goes for a walk along the water at two in the morning, is checking it without knowing. In Terminal City their movement is what keeps the edge in place: a person tracing the city's edge, again and again, holds that edge where it is. When the movement thins out, a stretch of path can start to drift, or a lamp repeats itself farther around the bend than it should. The rule is the shortest one in the city. Keep moving.

Two friends walk the seawall. One is timing a loop; the other keeps stopping to look over the water. After the third stop, the timer goes ahead and reaches a lamp with a peeled patch of paint they are certain they have already passed. They photograph it and hurry on, only to find the same patch again. The slower friend catches up, unimpressed by the evidence, and offers the remaining half of a snack. They put the phone away and walk together at an ordinary pace. The next lamp has no peeled patch. Neither turns back to test it. A small raccoon retreats among the roots beside the path, occupied with its own evening. Their conversation resumes where the argument had interrupted it.

The ruleKeep moving.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
